en: What does the team that wins the coin toss get to choose before kick-off?
es: ¿Qué puede elegir el equipo que gana el volado antes del saque inicial?
cs: El equipo que gana el coin toss, ¿qué le toca escoger, el lado de la cancha o el kick-off?
answer: The toss winner picks either which goal to attack in the first half or to take the kick-off, and the other team gets whichever option is left.
note: L8.1.1 opens with the coin toss and the two choices available to the winner.

en: Can you be offside from a throw-in?
es: ¿Hay fuera de juego en un saque de banda?
cs: ¿Te pueden marcar offside directo de un throw-in?
answer: No. There is no offside offence when a player receives the ball directly from a throw-in, and the same goes for a goal kick and a corner kick.
note: L11.3 lists the three restarts from which receiving the ball directly is never an offside offence.

en: Can a player who got a red card during the match take a kick in the penalty shoot-out?
es: ¿Un jugador que fue expulsado durante el partido puede tirar en la tanda de penales?
cs: Si a un jugador le sacaron la roja during the game, ¿todavía puede tirar en los penalties?
answer: No. A player sent off during the match may not take part in the shoot-out.
note: L10.3.0 states that a player sent off during the match is not permitted to take part in the shoot-out.

en: How far away do opponents have to stand from the player taking a throw-in?
es: ¿A qué distancia tienen que estar los rivales del que hace el saque de banda?
cs: En un throw-in, ¿qué tan lejos tiene que pararse el defender del que saca?
answer: At least 2 m (2 yds) from the point on the touchline where the throw-in is to be taken.
note: L15.1 sets the 2 m minimum distance in the throw-in procedure; also: L15.2, which repeats the distance when describing the sanction.

en: On a corner kick, does the ball have to leave the corner area before it is in play?
es: En un tiro de esquina, ¿el balón tiene que salir del cuadrante para estar en juego?
cs: En un corner kick, ¿la pelota tiene que salir del corner area para que ya esté in play?
answer: No. The ball is in play as soon as it is kicked and clearly moves; it does not need to leave the corner area.
note: L17.1 says when the ball is in play at a corner kick and that leaving the corner area is not required.

en: How far back does the wall have to be at a free kick?
es: ¿A qué distancia tiene que ponerse la barrera en un tiro libre?
cs: En un free kick, ¿a cuántas yardas tiene que estar la barrera from the ball?
answer: Opponents must stay at least 9.15 m (10 yds) from the ball until it is in play, unless they are standing on their own goal line between the goalposts.
note: L13.2 gives the required distance for opponents at every free kick and its goal line exception; also: L13.3, which cites the same distance when describing the sanction.

en: Does the goalkeeper have to stay on the goal line during a penalty kick?
es: ¿El portero tiene que quedarse sobre la línea de gol en un penal?
cs: En un penal, ¿el goalie tiene que quedarse on the line hasta que le peguen al balón?
answer: Yes. The goalkeeper stays on the goal line between the posts, facing the kicker, until the ball is kicked, and at the moment of the kick must have at least part of one foot touching, in line with, or behind the goal line.
note: L14.1 contains both the requirement to remain on the goal line until the kick and the one foot rule at the moment of the kick; the consequences of breaking it are in L14.2.

en: When the assistant with the flag decides whether a striker had run too far ahead of the defenders, does an elbow or a sleeve sticking out in front matter?
es: Cuando el abanderado decide si un delantero se había ido demasiado adelante de los defensas, ¿importa que solo le sobresalga el codo o la manga?
cs: Cuando el linesman decide si el delantero was too far ahead de los defensas, ¿cuenta si nomás el codo is sticking out?
answer: No. Hands and arms are ignored for every player; only the head, body and feet count, and the arm is taken to start at the bottom of the armpit.
note: L11.1 defines which body parts are used to judge the position and excludes hands and arms; avoided: offside, position, player, head, body, feet, hands, arms, armpit, opponent, second-last, goal line, halfway line, ball, level (es: fuera de juego, posición, jugador, cabeza, tronco, pierna, manos, brazos, axila, adversario, penúltimo, línea, balón).

en: If a shot smacks the woodwork and bounces back onto the pitch, do they carry on or is there a stoppage?
es: Si un disparo pega en el palo y regresa a la cancha, ¿se sigue o se para el partido?
cs: Si el tiro pega en el palo and bounces back a la cancha, ¿siguen o lo paran?
answer: They carry on. The ball stays in play when it comes back off a goalpost, the crossbar or a corner flagpost and remains on the field.
note: L9.2 says the ball is still in play after coming off the goal frame or corner flagpost if it stays on the field; avoided: ball, in play, rebound, goalpost, crossbar, corner flagpost, remains, field of play, match official (es: balón, juego, rebote, poste, travesaño, banderín, permanezca, terreno).

en: Does it count if the man in gloves hurls it by hand from his own box all the way into the net at the far end with nobody else touching it?
es: ¿Cuenta el tanto si el arquero avienta la pelota con el brazo desde su área y se mete en el arco de enfrente sin que nadie más la toque?
cs: ¿Cuenta si el arquero la avienta from his own box y se mete all the way en el arco de enfrente?
answer: No. If the goalkeeper throws the ball directly into the opponents' goal, no goal is given and the other team gets a goal kick.
note: L10.1 has the specific sentence on a goalkeeper's throw going straight into the other goal; avoided: goal, scored, goalkeeper, throws, directly, opponents, goal kick, ball, awarded (es: gol, guardameta, lanza, mano, portería, directamente, contraria, saque de meta, balón).

en: When the whistle goes because somebody is hurt and there was no foul, which side is handed it back afterwards?
es: Cuando pitan para atender a un lesionado y no hubo falta, ¿a quién le devuelven la pelota al seguir?
cs: Cuando pitan porque alguien is hurt y no hubo foul, ¿a quién le dan la pelota when they start again?
answer: It is a dropped ball: for the defending goalkeeper if the ball was inside the penalty area, otherwise for a player of the team that would have kept or won possession, or, if the referee cannot tell, the team that last touched it.
note: L8.2.1 sets out who receives a dropped ball depending on where the ball was when play stopped; also: L8.0 for why the restart is a dropped ball; avoided: dropped ball, referee, play, stopped, ball, team, player, possession, retained, gained, touched, penalty area, goalkeeper, restart (es: balón a tierra, árbitro, juego, detener, balón, equipo, jugador, posesión, conservado, ganado, tocó, área penal, guardameta, reanudación).

en: What gesture tells everyone that a set piece needs a second person involved before it can count, and when is the official allowed to drop that gesture?
es: ¿Con qué ademán avisa el silbante que en un cobro a pelota parada hace falta que alguien más intervenga para que valga la anotación, y hasta cuándo lo tiene que sostener?
cs: ¿Qué seña hace el silbante to let everyone know que en ese set piece alguien más tiene que intervenir before it counts, y cuándo la puede bajar?
answer: The referee raises an arm above the head and keeps it up until the kick has been taken and the ball touches another player, goes out of play, or it is clear a goal cannot be scored directly.
note: L13.1.1 describes the indirect free kick signal and how long it is held; avoided: referee, indicates, indirect, free kick, raising, arm, head, signal, maintained, taken, ball, touches, player, goal, scored, directly (es: árbitro, indicar, tiro libre, indirecto, levantar, brazo, cabeza, señal, mantener, balón, toque, jugador, gol, marcar, directamente).

en: From twelve yards, may the shooter pause at the end of his approach and pretend to strike, sending the man between the sticks the wrong way, before actually hitting it?
es: Desde los once pasos, ¿puede el cobrador frenarse al terminar su impulso y amagar el disparo para engañar al arquero antes de pegarle a la pelota?
cs: Desde los once pasos, ¿el cobrador puede frenarse at the end of his approach y amagar para engañar al arquero, or is that not allowed?
answer: No. A dummy during the run-up is allowed, but feinting to kick once the run-up is finished is an offence: the referee restarts with an indirect free kick for the defending team whether or not the ball went in, and cautions the kicker.
note: L14.2 lists feinting after completing the run-up among the kicker offences that always lead to an indirect free kick and a caution; avoided: penalty, kick, kicker, feinting, run-up, completed, goalkeeper, ball, goal, cautions, indirect free kick, referee (es: penal, tiro, ejecutor, lanzador, finta, carrera, finalizado, guardameta, balón, golpear, portería, amonestar, libre indirecto, árbitro).

en: When someone on the sideline stalls instead of putting it back in, just to burn the clock, what does the official do, and can their rivals wind up with it?
es: Cuando alguien hace tiempo en el lateral y no acaba de meterla a la cancha, ¿qué hace el juez y se la pueden dar al rival?
cs: Cuando alguien está wasting time en el lateral y no la mete, ¿qué hace el juez, and can their rivals wind up with it?
answer: The referee whistles and starts a visible five-second countdown with a raised hand; if the throw-in has not been taken when it runs out, the throw-in goes to the opposing team. The player is only cautioned for excessive further delay after that.
note: L15.2 describes the five-second countdown for a delayed throw-in and the switch of the throw to the opponents; avoided: throw-in, delaying, unfairly, taking, player, team, referee, whistle, signal, five seconds, countdown, raised hand, awarded, opposing, cautioned, ball (es: saque de banda, retrasar, ejecución, jugador, equipo, árbitro, silbato, señalar, cuenta atrás, cinco segundos, mano levantada, conceder, adversario, amonestar, balón).

en: A midfielder's pass strikes the referee in the centre circle and rolls to an opponent, who sets off on a counter-attack. Does play go on, and if not, how does it restart?
es: El pase de un mediocampista le pega al árbitro en el círculo central y el balón le queda a un rival, que arranca un contragolpe. ¿Sigue la jugada? Si no, ¿cómo se reanuda?
cs: El pase le pega al ref en media cancha y la pelota le queda al otro equipo, que se va en counter-attack. ¿Sigue el juego or does the ref stop it, y cómo se reanuda?
answer: Play does not go on. The ball is out of play because it touched a match official, stayed on the field and the team in possession changed, and play restarts with a dropped ball.
note: L9.1 lists a ball that touches a match official followed by a change of possession as out of play and names the dropped ball restart; also: L8.2.1 for who receives the dropped ball.

en: A through ball is played toward a striker standing behind the back line. A centre back with time and a clear view swings a foot to clear it, mishits it, and it runs straight to that striker, who scores. Does the goal stand?
es: Mandan un pase filtrado hacia un delantero que está detrás de la línea defensiva. Un central, con tiempo y viendo bien el balón, intenta despejar con el pie, le pega mal y se lo deja al delantero, que anota. ¿Vale el gol?
cs: Mandan un through ball a un delantero que está behind the back line. El central, con tiempo y viéndola clarito, tries to clear it, le pega mal y se la deja al delantero, que mete gol. ¿Vale o es offside?
answer: Yes. The defender deliberately played the ball, and a failed clearance still counts as deliberate play, which means the striker is not treated as having gained an advantage from the offside position.
note: L11.2 covers receiving the ball from an opponent's deliberate play, says an unsuccessful clearance is still deliberate, and gives the time and clear view indicators.

en: After a sliding tackle, a defender ends up off the pitch behind his own goal line and stays there without the referee's permission. Seconds later a pass reaches an attacker who has only the goalkeeper between him and that goal line. Is the attacker offside?
es: Tras una barrida, un defensa queda fuera de la cancha, detrás de su propia línea de meta, y se queda ahí sin permiso del árbitro. Segundos después le llega un pase a un atacante que solo tiene al portero entre él y esa línea. ¿Está en fuera de juego?
cs: Después de una barrida, el defensa se queda off the field, detrás de su goal line, sin permiso del ref. Luego le llega el pase a un atacante que nomás tiene al portero enfrente. ¿Es offside o no?
answer: No. A defender who leaves the field without permission is treated as standing on the goal line for offside until the next stoppage or until his team plays the ball out of its penalty area towards halfway, which leaves two opponents (the goalkeeper and that defender) not behind the attacker.
note: L11.4 has the rule that a defender off the field without permission counts as being on the goal line for offside; the general definition of the position is in L11.1.

en: The referee restarts with a dropped ball for a midfielder near the halfway line. As soon as it hits the ground he shoots from distance, and the ball flies into the opponents' goal without anyone else touching it. What is the decision?
es: El árbitro reanuda con un balón a tierra para un mediocampista cerca de la media cancha. En cuanto bota, el jugador dispara de lejos y el balón entra en la portería rival sin que nadie más lo toque. ¿Qué se marca?
cs: El ref hace un dropped ball para un mediocampista cerca de media cancha. He shoots right away y la pelota entra al arco rival sin que nadie más la toque. ¿Cuenta el gol o qué marcan?
answer: No goal. A dropped ball must touch at least two players before it can go in, and because it entered the opponents' goal the restart is a goal kick.
note: L8.2.2 gives the two-player requirement after a dropped ball and the goal kick restart when it enters the opponents' goal.

en: A cup final goes to a penalty shoot-out. One team finished extra time with ten players because of a red card, and the other still has eleven. What has to happen before the kicks begin?
es: Una final se va a la tanda de penales. Un equipo terminó los tiempos extra con diez jugadores por una expulsión y el otro sigue con once. ¿Qué tiene que pasar antes de que empiecen a tirar?
cs: La final se va a penalties. Un equipo acabó el extra time con diez por una roja y el otro tiene once. ¿Qué tienen que hacer before the shoot-out starts?
answer: The team with eleven must drop to ten by excluding one player and must tell the referee that player's name and number. The excluded player takes no part in the kicks, other than possibly replacing a goalkeeper who cannot continue.
note: L10.3.1 requires the team with more players to reduce to the same number as its opponents and to inform the referee of each excluded player.

en: A team is fouled in midfield and takes the free kick at once. A defender standing only about four yards away sticks out a leg and intercepts the pass. Does the referee order a retake?
es: A un equipo le cometen falta en media cancha y cobra el tiro libre de inmediato. Un defensa que estaba a unos cuatro metros estira la pierna e intercepta el pase. ¿El árbitro manda repetir el tiro?
cs: Les hacen falta en media cancha y cobran el free kick rapidito. Un defensa que estaba like four yards away mete la pierna y corta el pase. ¿El ref lo manda repetir or play on?
answer: No, play continues. When a free kick is taken quickly and an opponent closer than 9.15 m (10 yds) intercepts it, the referee lets play go on.
note: L13.3 has the quick free kick exception to the retake for an opponent inside the required distance.

en: A winger taking a corner taps the ball a yard out of the corner area and then dribbles it himself toward the box before any other player has touched it. What does the referee give?
es: Un extremo cobra un tiro de esquina, toca el balón un metro fuera del cuadrante y luego él mismo se lo lleva hacia el área antes de que lo toque otro jugador. ¿Qué marca el árbitro?
cs: El extremo cobra el corner, la toca tantito y luego he dribbles it himself hacia el área antes de que alguien más la toque. ¿Qué marca el ref?
answer: An indirect free kick to the defending team, because the kicker touched the ball a second time before it had touched another player.
note: L17.2 gives the indirect free kick for a corner taker who touches the ball again before another player does.

en: Can a goal be scored straight from a throw-in, and what about straight from a corner kick?
es: ¿Se puede meter gol directo de un saque de banda? ¿Y directo de un tiro de esquina?
cs: ¿Se puede meter gol directo from a throw-in? ¿Y de un corner kick, el gol olímpico sí vale?
answer: Not from a throw-in: if the ball goes straight into the opponents' goal it is a goal kick. From a corner kick yes, but only against the opposing team.
note: L15.0 says a goal cannot be scored directly from a throw-in and L17.0 says one can be scored directly from a corner kick; each half of the question needs its own passage.

en: If a player somehow sends the ball straight into his own team's goal from a kick-off, or straight from a free kick, is it an own goal in either case?
es: Si un jugador manda el balón directo a su propia portería en un saque inicial, o directo de un tiro libre, ¿cuenta como autogol en alguno de los dos casos?
cs: Si alguien manda la pelota straight into his own goal en el saque inicial, o directo de un free kick, ¿es autogol in either case?
answer: No in both cases. Whether it comes from a kick-off or from a direct or indirect free kick, a ball kicked directly into the kicker's own goal gives a corner kick to the opponents.
note: L8.1.1 covers the kick-off going directly into the kicker's own goal and L13.1.2 covers the same for free kicks; the two restarts are in different laws.

en: A defender's clearance hits the referee inside the defender's own penalty area and drops to an attacker a few yards away, still in the area. What does the referee do, and who gets the ball at the restart?
es: El despeje de un defensa le pega al árbitro dentro del área del propio defensa y el balón le cae a un atacante ahí mismo, todavía en el área. ¿Qué hace el árbitro y a quién le toca el balón en la reanudación?
cs: El despeje del defensa le pega al ref inside his own box y la pelota le cae a un atacante, todavía en el área. ¿Qué hace el ref, y quién se queda con la pelota on the restart?
answer: The referee stops play, because the ball touched a match official and possession changed, and restarts with a dropped ball. Since the ball was inside the penalty area, it is dropped for the defending team's goalkeeper.
note: L9.1 makes the ball out of play with a dropped ball restart after it hits the referee and possession changes, and L8.2.1 says a dropped ball inside the penalty area goes to the defending goalkeeper.

en: During a penalty shoot-out, where does each of the two goalkeepers have to be while a kick is taken: the one facing the kick and the one whose team-mate is taking it?
es: En una tanda de penales, ¿dónde tiene que colocarse cada uno de los dos porteros mientras se tira: el que ataja y el del equipo que está tirando?
cs: En los penalties, ¿dónde se tiene que parar cada portero while the kick is taken: el que ataja y el del equipo que está tirando?
answer: The goalkeeper facing the kick stays on the goal line between the posts, facing the kicker, until the ball is kicked. The kicker's own goalkeeper waits on the field outside the penalty area, on the goal line where it meets the penalty area boundary line.
note: L14.1 gives the defending goalkeeper's position at a penalty kick, which applies in the shoot-out, and L10.3.1 gives the position of the kicker's goalkeeper.

en: A goalkeeper catches a cross and holds on to the ball for well over eight seconds. What does the referee award, and from which side of the field is it taken?
es: Un portero atrapa un centro y se queda con el balón en las manos bastante más de ocho segundos. ¿Qué marca el árbitro y desde qué lado de la cancha se cobra?
cs: El portero atrapa un centro y se queda con la pelota way more than eight seconds. ¿Qué marca el ref, y de qué lado se cobra?
answer: A corner kick to the opponents, taken from the corner area nearest to where the goalkeeper was when penalised.
note: L12.3 awards a corner kick when a goalkeeper controls the ball with the hands for more than eight seconds and L17.1 says which corner area is used; also: L17.0 for the award itself.
